title: Mothership shift — lull protocol notebook
content:
Quick context
This is a personal working notebook for the "mothership shift" — a plan to flip the primary routing plane to the new runtime variant with a deliberately low-traffic "lull" period first. Not for broad consumption yet; notes, heuristics, and ad-hoc queries.

Objective
- Flip production default model-serving variant with minimal customer impact.
- Use an extended low-pressure soak (the 'lull') to validate tail latencies, KV cache stability, and edge fallbacks before any significant traffic transfer.
- Provide clear metrics and escape hatches for fast rollback.

High-level phases
1) Baseline capture (48h)
   - Collect baseline SLO percentiles (p50/p95/p99), error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, and average token cost for current serving plane.
   - Save baseline snapshot with tag: mothership-baseline-YYYYMMDD.

2) Lighthouse (1h)
   - Send controlled synthetic requests (rich prompt variety) from 3 regions to validate request path and model variant compatibility.
   - Verify trace continuity and no silent truncation.

3) Lull period (72h recommended)
   - Route 0.5% of production traffic to new variant via SDK flag gating. Keep population stratified across tenants and request sizes.
   - Observe slow drift signals: cache warming, cold-start frequency, memory spikes.

4) Ramp window (24-72h)
   - If lull green, step traffic to 5% -> 20% -> 50% in discrete timeboxes with pause-and-observe in between.

5) Mothership flip (target window 2h quiet period)
   - If 50% stable for a sustained period and all safety checks pass, flip default routing for non-sensitive tiers and begin final monitoring.

Admission and guardrails (explicit)
- Hard abort if any of these fire during a phase:
  * error_rate_increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute AND sustained > 10 minutes
  * p99 latency regression vs baseline > 2x OR > 1.5s absolute increase for critical customers
  * KV cache hit ratio drop > 8 percentage points
  * memory OOMs or repeated container restarts

- Soft pause (manual review) triggers:
  * p95 increases by > 40% for more than 20 minutes
  * client-side QoS alerts (ingest-side requeues) observed

Cohort sampling matrix (how we pick the 0.5%)
- Percentiles of token length: 20% short (<50 tokens), 60% medium (50-400), 20% long (>400)
- Tenant risk bucket: 50% low-risk (internal tests & opt-in), 30% medium (early adopter tenants), 20% high-risk (enterprise)
- Region distribution: mirror production region weights but ensure at least one small sample from every region.

Flagging strategy (SDK + server-side)
- SDK flag key: runtime_variant=mothership_v2_lull
- Server-side router mapping: if header X-Experiment: mothership-lull -> route to variant pool A.
- Fallback: if variant pool A unavailable, server falls back to last-known-compatible variant with a circuit-breaker timeout of 2s.

Pseudocode for routing decision (concept)
- if tenant.in_holdlist -> force legacy
- elif request.has_header('X-Experiment', 'mothership-lull') -> try variantA
- elif random() < tenant_sampling_fraction -> route variantA
- else -> legacy

Telemetry snippets (promql-style, adapt as needed)
- error rate (per-minute): sum(rate(runtime_errors_total[1m])) by (variant) / sum(rate(runtime_requests_total[1m])) by (variant)
- p99 latency (ms): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, variant))
- kv cache hit ratio: sum(rate(kv_hits_total[5m])) by (variant) / (sum(rate(kv_hits_total[5m])) by (variant) + sum(rate(kv_misses_total[5m])) by (variant))
- cold starts: increase in container_starts_total[5m] per replica

Observability checklist (pre-lull)
- dashboard: baseline vs variant panes (latency, errors, cache, cost)
- traces: instrument synthetic lighthouse traces with clear span naming
- alerts: temporary alert thresholds for the experiment; notify #ops-release and on-call
- logging: ensure request id propagates and variant id included in logs

Runbook: immediate recovery flow
1) If hard abort condition -> flip SDK flag to legacy for all traffic and set router override: default -> legacy.
2) Notify SRE on-call, owners of serving-runtime, and the release lead.
3) Start triage: collect last 60 minutes of traces, top-10 slow traces, heap dumps of affected replicas.
4) If root cause identified and fix trivial (config, circuit-breaker mis-set), consider a targeted patch and lighthouse re-run.
5) If unknown or broad systemic, keep legacy routing and open incident.

Post-rollout watchlist (first 7 days)
- Daily run rate vs token cost delta by tenant
- Customer service inbound triage: map any reports to tenant buckets in cohort matrix
- Model output quality drift (sampled evals): A small evaluation harness should run at 1% sample of new variant outputs and compare to baseline prompts.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide exact length of lull (48h vs 72h). Longer helps KV steady-state but delays rollouts.
- Who owns the mothership flip window? (ops owns execution; release lead owns go/no-go)
- Need a small harness to auto-bisect long-tail latency regressions by prompt class.

Notes to self
- Keep communication terse: one Slack thread per phase.
- Prefer manual pauses between steps for first two flips; automation can be added after a couple successful runs.
- This is a personal checklist: will refine into a formal playbook after first successful mothership flip.

End of notebook

(appendix: example curl to opt a tenant in for the lull)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/flags/opt-in \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-corp","flag":"runtime_variant","value":"mothership_v2_lull"}'
